title: Give every hband screen (reader pages, /admin pages, Blocked users and the forbidden page) one designed look in light and dark, from one shared stylesheet and layout
how_to_read: Each attempt is one line and a `details` filename in this same directory. Open a detail file ONLY when this index points you at one -- the summaries are here so you do not have to. `caused_by` is what sent the stage back; `changed` is what the attempt then touched, counted by kind. Several attempts in a row that were caused by the same stage and changed no `src` is a loop, not progress.

open.issue: One shared design system in one place: colour tokens for light AND dark, a type scale and a spacing scale: missing

Components covering links, buttons, text inputs/textareas, forms and form rows, notices, lists and tables, cards/panels, details/summary, badges and avatars, plus the admin needs: tables, destructive buttons and the two-step remove: missing
One shared base layout that every template takes; no page carries its own head, style block or inline styles: partial

Every reader screen (home and /reports/<slug> with report frame, like count, vote controls, comments and the feedback box with the sender's own messages and author replies; the show-all page; the branch page), signed in and signed out, shows the designed look: missing

Every /admin screen (admin.html, admin_report.html, admin_blocked.html) and the forbidden page shows the designed look, with the admin components (tables, destructive buttons, two-step remove): missing
Dark mode follows prefers-color-scheme with no manual light/dark switch: missing
No control or link is left in the browser default (checked by computed styles, not screenshots): missing
No horizontal scroll at a true 375 CSS px phone width on every screen: partial
Text and controls meet a stated contrast bar in both schemes (WCAG AA proposed): partial
report-frame-canvas-under-site-surface: V1 light: report A shows site #f3f1ea inside the frame (not white); dark stays white. V2 flips B.
Thread script: kept in the head behind a ThreadScript() method, giving byte-identical reader pages (practice, chosen), or the tag moved into main, giving a simpler data contract (crossdomain).
Header: inside page-start, so no page can forget it, with forbidden.html defining its own brand-only header (practice, chosen); or called by each page, with a shared "brand" partial (crossdomain).

Admin roles: class="primary" on Upload and class="danger" on Delete (practice), or frozen markup with form-action selectors (crossdomain, chosen). Neither button is pinned by a test, so this is a judgement of explicitness against one uniform 'bodies unchanged' rule.
Head: add `<meta name="color-scheme" content="light dark">` to avoid a white flash before the CSS loads (crossdomain), or keep the head verbatim for byte identity (practice, chosen).
Hidden states: a structural [hidden]:not(:target) guard (crossdomain, chosen), or a source check banning display on hidden-carrying hooks (practice).

internal/layout as a package (both, chosen), or practice's flagged trim: forbidden.html keeps its own head, pinned byte-equal to the server's "head", with no new package and no test edit, at the cost of the brief's 'no page carries its own head' bar.
Decoration: an avatar ring drawn with an opaque box-shadow and a CSS-border chevron on summaries. These are left to the frontend designer within the token contract.

The seeded launcher was not extended with an owner session, a draft report, feedback with author replies and a blocked account (design plan item 11). Its browser sign-in is the stand-in's octocat, a non-owner, and its tests pin the nine-comment e004-look seed. So /admin, /admin/reports/<slug> and /admin/blocked are not in `screens` (it also holds at most 6). TestEveryScreenIsDesigned measures all of them as the owner, light and dark, at 1280 and 375, with details open, and I looked at their screenshots.
Firefox and Safari were not run (O-017, owed to validate): only Chrome is driven here.
Delete this report permanently has no confirmation step; it is a one-step filled danger button. A confirmation would be new behaviour and stays filed for a person.
The engine's own Fitness op=check with its real YAML parser was not run; the builder cannot. This attempt did not touch .taad/fitness.yaml, and TestRulesHoldOnTheTree passes.

With --bg #ffffff and #131416 now almost exactly Chrome's own canvas (#ffffff, #121212), TestReportFrameKeepsItsOwnCanvas can no longer tell `iframe { background-color: Canvas }` from the site surface showing through: removing the Canvas line would still pass. The test's control (A under dark, outside #131416 against inside #ffffff) still shows it can see differences. A row that serves a stylesheet with a different --bg would pin it again.

Q-012's decided enforcement (a fitness rule forbidding `<script` in report.html and layout.html) does not exist in fitness.yaml, and thread.js loads on the found home, report and branch pages. The tag now lives in internal/layout/templates/base.html and is pinned there by TestEveryPageTakesTheShell. A person should say whether Q-012 is amended to 'thread.js is the one allowed site script'.

The engine's projects.app_command still has to be repointed to `go run ./internal/testutil/seeded -port {port}`. To photograph the admin screens, the seeded launcher needs a way to sign in as the owner (fakegithub SetUser on the serving program) and a draft, feedback with replies and a blocked account in its seed.

Cross-rule ordering of border shorthands (a later rule restating `border: 1px solid` after another rule set border-color to a token) is caught only inside one rule. A browser assertion that every bordered control's edge colour differs from its text colour would close it.
Architecture: internal/server (C-001) also imports internal/layout (C-008); only the C-002 edge fits in this report's three edits.

deviation: admin_report.html: 'Nothing visible on this report.' keeps its bare

and is styled through `.moderation > h2 + p:last-child`, not class="empty-inline" as the plan said, because remove_test.go:731 pins the exact string `

Nothing visible on this report.

`. The plan's own rule is to bind by selector where a test pins the markup. The other empty notes got their classes.

deviation: probe.js exempts `.admin-nav a` from the 3:1 control-boundary check. The sidebar's current page is marked by weight and a --surface-2 tint (1.1:1 against the page, by the look's own tokens), which is state, not a control edge. The link text is still judged for 4.5:1, the current item's fill is role-checked, and the sidebar is checked to be one row inside 375 px.

deviation: The plan's note that /admin 'keeps its own owner line and Sign out' (filed for a person in the first design) is superseded: this look's plan deletes the owner line, Sign out and back links from admin.html, and the shared header and sidebar carry them. main_test.go still finds @the-owner in /admin through the header's 'Signed in as'.

deviation: internal/testutil/seeded is unchanged, so the app command seeds the e004-look thread and signs in as a non-owner only. The plan asked for an owner session, a draft, feedback with replies and a blocked account in the seed; I did not extend it (see not_built).

deviation: This build contains no workaround for a defect outside the project, so there is no per-bug checkbox or notice to build. The accepted finding M-add-1 still holds: every edge is a literal width and style plus a *-color longhand, so an engine without light-dark() draws currentColor edges and no fills.

drift: site.css does not mute the help paragraphs of the Upload and Replace sections. The look says the Upload a report section is 'an admin h2, the muted help, and the upload form' and that Replace has 'muted help and the upload form card'. internal/server/static/site.css:255 (`.upload > p, .upload > form, form[action='/admin/reports'] { max-width: 44rem; }`) sets only a width, so admin.html's 'One self-contained .html file…' paragraph and admin_report.html's 'Uploading under this slug…' paragraph render in --text at body size. Only the code hint inside the form is muted (line 261).

caused_by.reason: Restarted from build-slice by a person: The owner wants a different look: Ghost-like in spirit, without the bloat. The reader pages (a thread, All reports) read like an editorial publication: confident headline type, a roomy reading measure, calm generous spacing, and All reports as a clean list of titles with their date and status. The /admin pages work like a quiet publishing admin: a left sidebar (Reports, Blocked users, View site), a reports list with status pills, and each page's main action at the top right. No bloat: one stylesheet, system fonts only, no web fonts, no script beyond thread.js. Take Ghost's qualities only, never its theme, brand, assets or code. Everything the slice already owes still holds: light and dark, WCAG AA contrast, and Blocked users and the forbidden page on the same look.
